title: Glossy Candied Orange and Lemon Peel
summary: Strips of orange and lemon peel blanched three times to tame their bitterness, then simmered slowly in syrup until soft, glossy and translucent.
equipment: wire rack set over a tray

ingredients.item: orange peel, from about 3 large thick-skinned oranges
ingredients.note: keep the fruit for another use

steps.title: Cut the peel
steps.text: Score each orange and lemon from top to bottom into quarters and pull the peel away from the fruit. Slice it into strips about 6 mm wide and trim off any thick white pith or bits of flesh.

steps.title: Blanch three times
steps.text: Put the strips in the saucepan and cover them with cold water. Bring to the boil, boil for 5 min and drain. Do this twice more, with fresh cold water each time; each round takes away more bitterness.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Put the sugar, the 400 ml water and the corn syrup in the empty pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has completely dissolved.

steps.title: Simmer until translucent
steps.text: Add the blanched peel and bring back to the boil, then turn the heat down so the syrup barely bubbles. Simmer for 40-60 min, stirring now and then, until the strips are soft and look translucent, especially at the edges.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Lift the strips out with a fork, letting the excess syrup drip back into the pan, and lay them in a single layer on the paper-lined rack.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Leave uncovered at room temperature for 8-12 h, until the peel is glossy but no longer wet or sticky to touch.

tips: The most common mistake is skipping a blanch; the peel stays harsh and bitter, so do all three rounds.
Keep the syrup at a bare simmer; a hard boil caramelises the sugar and toughens the peel.
For a sparkly finish, toss the dried strips in granulated sugar.
Save the leftover syrup; it is lovely in iced tea, lemonade or brushed over cakes.
storage: Keep in an airtight jar at room temperature for up to 1 month, or in the fridge for up to 3 months.
